answer: A sybil ring dies at the one memory it cannot buy: a per-epoch "cedar" ledger that binds each identity to work it must re-forge every round from an unpredictable seed. Sybils pay that toll once per synthetic wallet, so their cost scales linearly while a single honest agent pays it once. Each join also names a distinct physical "canyon" — the same canyon cannot be claimed twice within one epoch — so a thousand cloned keys collapse onto one lane and are turned away with the seam still visible.
